title: Pre-eclampsia, severe hypertension in pregnancy and eclampsia
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
setting: Antenatal clinic, labour room, emergency department, obstetric HDU
summary: Treat BP of 160/110 mmHg or more within 30 to 60 minutes (IV labetalol, oral nifedipine or IV hydralazine), give magnesium sulphate for severe features or eclampsia (Pritchard or Zuspan), and plan birth: 37 weeks without severe features, 34 weeks with severe features, after stabilisation for eclampsia.

sections.title: Diagnose and grade (ACOG 2020)
items: Gestational hypertension: BP 140/90 mmHg or more on two occasions at least 4 hours apart after 20 weeks in a previously normotensive woman. Severe range is systolic 160 or more or diastolic 110 or more; confirm within 15 minutes and treat, do not wait 4 hours.

Pre-eclampsia: that hypertension plus proteinuria (300 mg or more per 24 hours, urine protein:creatinine ratio 0.3 mg/mg (30 mg/mmol) or more, or dipstick 2+ if no quantitative test), OR new organ dysfunction even without proteinuria.

Severe features: BP 160/110 or more; platelets below 100,000/microlitre; transaminases above twice normal or severe persistent right upper quadrant or epigastric pain; creatinine above 1.1 mg/dL or doubled; pulmonary oedema; new headache not relieved by analgesia; visual disturbance.
HELLP: haemolysis (LDH 600 IU/L or more), AST or ALT above twice the upper limit, platelets below 100,000/microlitre. Up to 15% have no hypertension or proteinuria and about 30% present after birth.

Eclampsia: new tonic-clonic seizures with no other cause. Consider alternatives (cerebral venous thrombosis, haemorrhage, epilepsy, hypoglycaemia) if seizures start more than 48 to 72 hours postpartum or occur despite magnesium.

sections.title: Eclamptic seizure: immediate steps
items: Call for help. Left lateral position, protect from injury, clear the airway, suction, oxygen, SpO2 monitoring. Do not use diazepam or phenytoin as first-line; give the magnesium sulphate loading dose.
IV access; send CBC with platelets, creatinine, LFT, LDH, coagulation screen, group and save; urinary catheter for hourly output.
Recurrent seizure while on magnesium: a further 2 g IV over 5 minutes (NICE allows 2 to 4 g).
Treat severe BP (next section) and restrict total IV fluid to 80 mL/h unless there are ongoing losses such as haemorrhage.

Deliver once the mother is stabilised (seizures controlled, BP treated, oxygenation adequate), whatever the gestation. Mode of birth follows obstetric indications; vaginal birth is not contraindicated.
Where the full magnesium regimen cannot be given (for example primary care), give the loading dose and transfer immediately to a higher facility (WHO 2011).

sections.title: Severe hypertension (160/110 or more): treat within 30 to 60 minutes
items: Any of IV labetalol, oral immediate-release nifedipine or IV hydralazine is acceptable; lower BP promptly but gradually and monitor the fetus. Once controlled, aim for about 135/85 mmHg on maintenance treatment (NICE NG133).

Labetalol IV: 20 mg over 2 minutes; recheck BP at 10 minutes and, if still severe, give 40 mg, then 80 mg at 10-minute intervals; maximum cumulative 300 mg, then change agent. Alternative infusion 1 to 2 mg/min. Avoid in asthma, heart failure, heart block or bradycardia.

Nifedipine immediate-release oral: 10 mg; recheck at 20 minutes and, if still severe, 20 mg, then 20 mg again after a further 20 minutes; if still uncontrolled switch to IV labetalol. Maximum 180 mg/day (ACOG); FOGSI limits acute dosing to 120 mg. Swallow whole; never sublingual or bitten.

Hydralazine: 5 mg IV (or IM), then 5 to 10 mg IV every 20 to 40 minutes, maximum cumulative 20 mg IV (30 mg IM); or infusion 0.5 to 10 mg/h. Causes more maternal hypotension, headache and abnormal fetal heart tracings than the alternatives.
BP still severe after appropriate doses of two agents: urgent anaesthetic, critical care and senior obstetric input.
Maintenance: oral labetalol 200 mg twice daily, increased up to 800 mg every 8 to 12 hours (maximum 2400 mg/day); add or use extended-release nifedipine; methyldopa if both are unsuitable.

sections.title: Magnesium sulphate (MgSO4)
items: Indications: eclampsia, and pre-eclampsia or gestational hypertension with severe features, for prevention of seizures. Continue for 24 hours after birth or after the last seizure, whichever is later; at caesarean, run it before, during and for 24 hours after surgery.

Pritchard (IM) regimen, preferred in India (FOGSI): loading 4 g IV as 20 mL of 20% solution over 4 to 5 minutes, PLUS 10 g IM (5 g of 50% solution deep IM in each buttock, with 1 mL of 2% lignocaine in the syringe); total loading 14 g. Maintenance 5 g of 50% deep IM every 4 hours in alternate buttocks.
Zuspan (IV) regimen: 4 g IV over 5 to 15 minutes, then 1 g/h IV infusion by pump. ACOG uses 4 to 6 g over 20 to 30 minutes then 1 to 2 g/h.

Before each IM dose (or hourly on an infusion) confirm: respiratory rate above 16/min, patellar reflexes present, urine output above 100 mL in the last 4 hours. If any is not met, withhold the next dose and reassess.
Renal impairment or oliguria: give the full loading dose, but reduce maintenance (1 g/h per ACOG) and measure serum magnesium every 4 hours; stop the infusion if it exceeds 9.6 mg/dL (8 mEq/L).

sections.title: Monitoring and magnesium toxicity
items: BP every 15 to 30 minutes until below 160/110 mmHg; hourly urine output and fluid balance; SpO2 and respiratory rate; symptoms of headache, visual change and epigastric pain.

Magnesium toxicity: patellar reflexes are lost at about 9 mg/dL (7 mEq/L), respiratory depression at about 12 mg/dL (10 mEq/L), cardiac arrest at about 30 mg/dL (25 mEq/L). Routine serum levels are not needed if clinical checks are done.
Antidote: stop magnesium, give oxygen, support ventilation, and give calcium gluconate 10% 10 mL IV slowly over 3 to 10 minutes with ECG monitoring.

Blood tests in pre-eclampsia: CBC with platelets, renal and liver function twice a week if BP is below 160/110 and 3 times a week if 160/110 or more (NICE); more often (daily or as needed) with HELLP or deterioration.
Fetal surveillance: growth scan, liquor volume, umbilical artery Doppler and CTG as indicated.

sections.title: Timing of birth and postpartum care
items: Gestational hypertension or pre-eclampsia without severe features: deliver at 37+0 weeks (ACOG, FOGSI).
Severe features at 34+0 weeks or more: deliver after maternal stabilisation; do not delay birth for corticosteroids.

Severe features before 34 weeks with stable mother and fetus: expectant management only in a centre with maternal critical care and NICU; give antenatal corticosteroids. If the fetus is not viable, deliver after stabilisation.
During expectant management deliver for BP uncontrolled on 3 classes of drugs, SpO2 below 90%, eclampsia, pulmonary oedema, worsening renal, liver or platelet results, abruption, or fetal compromise.

Postpartum: eclampsia and stroke can occur after discharge. Check BP at least 4 times a day as an inpatient and at least once between days 3 and 5; treat if 150/100 mmHg or more (NICE). Enalapril is suitable during breastfeeding (NICE). NSAIDs may still be used for analgesia (ACOG 2020).
Counsel about recurrence and lifelong cardiovascular risk; arrange annual BP checks.

sections.title: Prevention in the next or current pregnancy
items: Low-dose aspirin for any high-risk factor (previous pre-eclampsia, chronic hypertension, CKD, SLE or antiphospholipid syndrome, type 1 or 2 diabetes, multifetal pregnancy) or more than one moderate factor (first pregnancy, age 35 or more, BMI above 30, family history of pre-eclampsia).
Aspirin dose: 75 to 150 mg once daily (NICE, FOGSI; ACOG uses 81 mg, WHO 75 mg), started from 12 weeks and ideally before 16 weeks (ACOG allows up to 28 weeks), continued until birth.
Calcium where dietary intake is low (most of India): WHO 1.5 to 2 g elemental calcium daily; FOGSI 1 to 1.5 g daily.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Delaying treatment of confirmed severe BP beyond 60 minutes, or ignoring isolated severe systolic hypertension (stroke risk).
Sublingual or bitten nifedipine causing a precipitous fall in BP and fetal distress.
Stopping magnesium before 24 hours postpartum, or using diazepam instead of magnesium.
Liberal IV fluids leading to pulmonary oedema.
Methylergometrine for PPH in a woman with pre-eclampsia.
Missing HELLP presenting as epigastric pain with near-normal BP, or postpartum pre-eclampsia presenting with headache after discharge.

drugs.name: Labetalol (IV)
drugs.dose: 20 mg IV over 2 minutes, then 40 mg, then 80 mg at 10-minute intervals if BP stays 160/110 or more; maximum cumulative 300 mg. Or infusion 1 to 2 mg/min
drugs.notes: Avoid in asthma, heart failure, heart block, bradycardia.

drugs.name: Nifedipine immediate-release (oral)
drugs.dose: 10 mg orally; if still severe at 20 minutes give 20 mg, repeat 20 mg after 20 minutes; maximum 180 mg/day
drugs.notes: Swallow whole. Never sublingual. Maintenance with extended-release nifedipine.

drugs.name: Hydralazine
drugs.dose: 5 mg IV or IM, then 5 to 10 mg IV every 20 to 40 minutes; maximum cumulative 20 mg IV or 30 mg IM. Infusion 0.5 to 10 mg/h
drugs.notes: More maternal hypotension and fetal heart rate abnormalities.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulphate (Pritchard)
drugs.dose: Loading 4 g IV (20% solution over 4 to 5 minutes) plus 5 g of 50% deep IM in each buttock; maintenance 5 g of 50% deep IM every 4 hours, alternate buttocks, for 24 hours after birth or last seizure
drugs.notes: Check respiratory rate above 16/min, patellar reflexes, urine above 100 mL per 4 hours before each dose.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulphate (Zuspan)
drugs.dose: Loading 4 g IV over 5 to 15 minutes, then 1 g/h IV infusion for 24 hours after birth or last seizure
drugs.notes: Recurrent seizure: further 2 g IV over 5 minutes. Reduce maintenance in renal impairment.

drugs.name: Calcium gluconate 10%
drugs.dose: 10 mL (1 g) IV slowly over 3 to 10 minutes
drugs.notes: Antidote for magnesium toxicity (respiratory depression, absent reflexes). ECG monitoring.

drugs.name: Labetalol (oral maintenance)
drugs.dose: 200 mg twice daily, increasing up to 800 mg every 8 to 12 hours; maximum 2400 mg/day

drugs.name: Aspirin (prophylaxis)
drugs.dose: 75 to 150 mg orally once daily from 12 weeks (ideally before 16 weeks) until birth
drugs.notes: For high-risk women or those with more than one moderate risk factor.
